text:
Pavel once pulled an all-nighter to stabilize a PostgreSQL cluster during a Black Friday traffic spike. He identified a query bottleneck, rewrote the logic using Redis for caching, and automated retries via GitHub Actions. The next morning, the system handled 3x normal traffic with 20% lower latency. His calm under pressure and knack for balancing urgency with precision made a real difference.  

Pavel is the kind of engineer who leaves the office at 5 PM but checks Slack at 5:05 to ensure a CI/CD pipeline isn’t hanging. He owns microservices at the API layer, ensuring REST endpoints are both resilient and easy to debug. His Linux admin skills shine in maintaining monitoring stacks—Prometheus and Grafana setups he fine-tunes to flag anomalies before they escalate. He’s equally comfortable writing Go for high-throughput services as he is configuring alerting rules to keep the team ahead of outages.  

What sets him apart is his ability to turn complexity into clarity. When we migrated a monolith to microservices, he designed a monitoring strategy that tracked service dependencies without overwhelming the team. His work on AWS infrastructure reduced provisioning time by 40%, and his chaos engineering experiments uncovered hidden bottlenecks in our CI/CD flows. He’s not just a problem solver—he’s a systems thinker who anticipates where things might break.  

Pavel’s technical depth and quiet reliability make him a standout. He’ll be a valuable asset to any team needing someone who can build, monitor, and scale systems with equal care.
